ing: such as sea bass or halibut, cut in 1-inch cubes
st: Boil the sweet potatoes for 20 minutes until tender, then peel and slice. Boil the corn for 10 minutes and cut into rounds.
Slice the red onion thinly, rinse in cold water for 1 minute, and drain.
Season the fish cubes with [[1.5 tsp]] salt in a glass bowl and rest for 2 minutes.
Add the garlic, aji amarillo paste and [[1 cup]] lime juice, then stir.
Add the ice cubes and stir for about 1 minute.
Let it sit for 5 to 8 minutes until the fish is opaque outside and tender inside.
Remove the ice, fold in the onion and [[0.25 cup]] cilantro.
Serve at once with the sweet potato and corn on the side, along with some of the lime marinade.

ing: about 2 cups for frying fries, rest for the wok
st: Fry the potato strips in [[2 cups]] oil at 350°F (175°C) for 8 minutes until golden, then drain and salt them.
Season the beef with [[1 tsp]] salt, pepper and cumin.
Heat a wok or large skillet over very high heat with [[2 tbsp]] oil.
Sear the beef in two batches for 2 minutes each until browned, then set aside.
In the same pan, stir-fry the garlic and aji amarillo for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and stir-fry for 2 minutes so it stays crisp.
Add the tomatoes and cook 1 minute.
Return the beef and pour in [[3 tbsp]] soy sauce and [[2 tbsp]] vinegar, tossing for 1 minute.
Fold in the fries and [[0.25 cup]] cilantro, and serve at once over rice.
Poach the chicken in lightly salted water for 20 minutes until it reaches 165°F (74°C). Reserve [[1 cup]] broth.
Shred the chicken with two forks.
Soak the bread in [[1 cup]] milk for 5 minutes, then blend it with the broth until smooth.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a pot, cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, aji paste and turmeric for 3 minutes.
Stir in the bread mixture and cook for 8 minutes until thickened.
Add the walnuts, Parmesan and [[1.5 tsp]] salt.
Fold in the shredded chicken and heat through for 5 minutes.
Serve over boiled potato slices with rice.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 25 minutes until tender, then drain, cool and peel.
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.
Blend the aji paste, cheese, milk, crackers, garlic, [[0.25 cup]] oil and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until smooth.
Add a splash of milk if it is too thick, and taste for salt.
Slice the potatoes and arrange them on lettuce leaves.
Pour the sauce over the potatoes.
Garnish with the halved eggs and olives and serve cool or at room temperature.
Crumble the cheese and break the crackers into pieces.
Add the cheese, crackers, aji paste and garlic to a blender.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] milk and blend until creamy.
With the blender running, slowly drizzle in [[0.25 cup]] oil until the sauce is thick and smooth.
Add [[1 tsp]] lime juice and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, blend and taste.
Thin with a little milk if you want it pourable, then chill briefly and serve over potatoes or eggs.
Trim off all fat and silver skin from the beef heart, then cut into 1-inch cubes.
Mix aji panca, garlic, vinegar, cumin, oregano, oil, salt and pepper into a marinade.
Toss the meat in the marinade, cover and chill for at least 4 hours.
Thread the meat on soaked skewers.
Heat a grill or grill pan to high heat.
Grill the skewers for 3 to 4 minutes per side, brushing with extra marinade for the first half only.
Stop when the meat is charred outside and cooked to at least 145°F (63°C).
Serve with boiled potatoes or corn.
Mix soy sauce, garlic, cumin, lime juice, paprika, beer, oil, oregano, pepper and salt into a marinade.
Pat the chicken dry. Rub the marinade over the skin and under it where you can.
Refrigerate, covered, for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and place the chicken on a rack in a roasting pan.
Roast for 20 minutes to brown the skin.
Lower the heat to 375°F (190°C) and roast 50 to 60 minutes more, until the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F (74°C).
Rest the chicken for 15 minutes before carving.
Serve with fries and a green sauce or salad.
Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water for 25 minutes until very soft, then drain and let steam dry.
Mash the potatoes until completely smooth, ideally with a ricer.
Knead in [[2 tbsp]] aji paste, [[3 tbsp]] lime juice, [[2 tbsp]] oil and [[1.5 tsp]] salt to make a soft dough, then chill 15 minutes.
Mix the chicken with [[0.5 cup]] mayonnaise and [[1 tbsp]] aji paste.
Line a square dish with plastic wrap. Press half the potato dough into an even layer.
Spread the chicken filling and top with sliced avocado.
Cover with the remaining potato dough and press flat.
Chill for 30 minutes, then unmold, slice and garnish with eggs and olives.
Blend the cilantro with [[0.5 cup]] beer or broth until it forms a smooth green puree.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt. Brown it in [[3 tbsp]] oil for 4 minutes per side, then set aside.
In the same pot, cook the onion, garlic, aji paste and cumin for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro puree and cook 4 minutes.
Add the rice, carrots, bell pepper and remaining salt and stir to coat.
Pour in [[2.5 cups]] broth and bring to a boil.
Return the chicken to the pot, cover and cook on low for 25 minutes.
Scatter the peas on top, cover and cook 5 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest 5 minutes and serve.

ing: or red bell peppers, tops cut off and seeded
2 for the custard, 1 hard-boiled and chopped
st: Blanch the peppers in boiling water with a pinch of sugar for 3 minutes. Repeat twice with fresh water to tame the heat, then drain.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, beef, cumin and [[1 tsp]] salt and cook 8 minutes, until the beef reaches 160°F (71°C).
Stir in the peanuts, raisins, olives and chopped egg and cool slightly.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Stuff the peppers with the filling and stand them upright in a baking dish.
Whisk the 2 eggs with [[0.75 cup]] milk and [[0.5 tsp]] salt and pour around the peppers.
Top the peppers with slices of cheese.
Bake 35 minutes until the custard sets and the cheese melts.
Boil the sweet potato and squash with the star anise in water for 25 minutes until soft. Save [[1 cup]] of the cooking water, then cool it.
Mash the cooked vegetables until smooth.
Dissolve the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] sugar in [[0.5 cup]] warm water and wait 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix the mash, yeast, [[2.5 cups]] flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, adding a little cooking water for a sticky, soft dough.
Cover and let rise for 1 hour until puffy.
Simmer the molasses with [[1 cup]] water, cinnamon and cloves for 15 minutes into a syrup, then strain.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil to 350°F (175°C).
With wet hands, take a handful of dough, poke a hole, and lower it into the oil as a ring.
Fry 2 minutes per side until golden. Drain and serve drizzled with the syrup.

ing: peel and core saved, plus chopped fruit
st: Rinse the corn and put it in a large pot with [[10 cups]] water.
Add the pineapple peel and core, apple, cinnamon sticks and cloves.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 45 minutes until the liquid is deep purple.
Strain through a fine sieve into a pitcher and discard solids.
Stir in [[0.75 cup]] sugar while the liquid is warm until dissolved.
Cool completely and stir in [[0.25 cup]] lime juice.
Chill for at least 1 hour and serve over ice with chopped pineapple.
